result.markdown: --- title: "[extract_status()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Extract the status codes from an event-time vector. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_event_time.py#L832-L858){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python extract_status(x) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A port of etd's `extract_status()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : An `EventTime` vector. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list of str or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One status code per element (`"e"`, `"r"`, `"l"`, or `"i"`), with `None` where it is missing. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#e29efcd1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw x = gw.event_time(time=[7, 5, 2], status=["e", "r", "i"], time_max=[None, None, 4]) gw.extract_status(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['e', 'r', 'i'] ``` ::: :::
